corrections.originalValue: Strongest feature: The move draws a logically important distinction between legendary shaping and personal existence, supports it with familiar narrative stereotypes, and directly protects the historical-person route from an inference that embellished or patterned stories necessarily imply a wholly invented subject. Principal limitation: Saying patterned construction has no bearing at all is broader than the examples justify, because the density, timing, provenance, and function of legendary material can affect evidential confidence even when legend never entails nonexistence by itself. Live burden: The case must show that recoverable, comparatively early evidence survives beneath or beside the patterns, rather than relying solely on the abstract compatibility of legend with a real person. Locked score: The very strong band recognizes a clear, relevant, and fundamentally sound non-entailment distinction, while withholding stronger appraisal because its categorical wording neglects how particular legendary patterns may still alter comparative historical probability.
